aws-c1-t01.title: What is Cloud Computing?
aws-c1-t01.definition: Cloud computing is on-demand delivery of computing resources (servers, storage, databases, networking, software) over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing.
aws-c1-t01.simpleExplanation: Apna server khareedne ki jagah internet par kiraye par computing lete hain, jitna use karo utna paisa do. Jab chahiye tab le lo, jab na chahiye chhod do.
aws-c1-t01.realLifeAnalogy: Electricity from the grid instead of running your own generator: you use it on demand and pay for what you consume.
aws-c1-t01.example: A startup launches a website on Amazon EC2 in minutes, handles a sale-day traffic spike by adding servers, and shuts them down afterwards — no hardware purchase.
keyPoints: NIST essential characteristics: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service.
Resources are shared (multi-tenant) and virtualised.
Pay-as-you-go instead of upfront capital cost.
Provider manages the physical infrastructure.
Scales up and down quickly.
Service models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS.
commonMistakes: Believing cloud means 'someone else's computer, no responsibility for you' — security is shared.
Thinking cloud always costs less regardless of usage.

examQuestions.question: Define cloud computing and its characteristics.
examQuestions.answer: On-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet; five NIST characteristics.

examQuestions.question: On-premises vs cloud.
examQuestions.answer: On-prem: buy/maintain hardware, fixed capacity; cloud: rent, elastic, pay per use.

knowledgeCheck.question: Cloud resources are billed per use.
A shop needs 10× servers only during Diwali. Cloud feature?
Capex vs opex.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Capex = upfront purchase; opex = ongoing pay-as-you-go.

aws-c1-t01.quickRevision: Cloud = on-demand IT over the internet, pay-as-you-go; 5 NIST traits (self-service, network, pooling, elasticity, measured).
aws-c1-t01.purpose: Remove the need to buy and maintain own infrastructure; give elastic, pay-per-use IT.
aws-c1-t01.scenario: E-commerce site scales servers up for a sale and down after, paying only for hours used.

aws-c1-t02.title: Key Benefits of Cloud Computing
aws-c1-t02.definition: The key benefits of cloud computing are trading upfront cost for variable cost, economies of scale, no capacity guessing, speed and agility, no data-centre maintenance and going global in minutes.
aws-c1-t02.simpleExplanation: Cloud ke fayde: kam upfront paisa, zyada scale par sasta, capacity ka andaza nahi lagana, jaldi launch, data centre ka jhanjhat nahi, aur duniya bhar me jaldi pahunchna.
aws-c1-t02.realLifeAnalogy: Renting a taxi when needed vs buying and maintaining your own car.
aws-c1-t02.example: A mobile app launches in 5 countries by deploying to five AWS Regions in a day, instead of building data centres.
keyPoints: Trade capital expense for variable expense.
Benefit from massive economies of scale (lower per-unit prices).
Stop guessing capacity: scale on demand.
Increase speed and agility: resources in minutes.
Stop spending on running and maintaining data centres.
Go global in minutes.
Also: high availability, reliability and security tools.
ifYouKnow: Choose a benefit for a scenario.
commonMistakes: Assuming cloud removes all security duties.
Forgetting that poor cost control can make cloud expensive.

examQuestions.question: Explain key benefits of cloud computing.
examQuestions.answer: Six advantages with examples.

examQuestions.question: What is economy of scale in cloud?
examQuestions.answer: Large providers get lower costs and pass savings through lower prices.

knowledgeCheck.question: Cloud needs you to guess capacity in advance.
Launching in a new country in a day. Benefit?
Agility vs elasticity.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Agility = speed of provisioning; elasticity = scaling with demand.

aws-c1-t02.quickRevision: Benefits: variable cost, economies of scale, no capacity guessing, agility, no DC upkeep, global in minutes.
aws-c1-t02.purpose: Explain why organisations migrate to the cloud.

aws-c1-t03.title: Cloud Service Models
aws-c1-t03.definition: Cloud service models define how much the provider manages: IaaS (infrastructure), PaaS (platform) and SaaS (software).
aws-c1-t03.simpleExplanation: IaaS me tum servers/OS khud sambhalte ho (EC2). PaaS me sirf apna code deploy karte ho (Elastic Beanstalk). SaaS me ready software use karte ho (Gmail).
aws-c1-t03.realLifeAnalogy: Pizza as a service: IaaS = you get kitchen and make pizza yourself; PaaS = ready dough, you add toppings; SaaS = ordering a finished pizza.
aws-c1-t03.example: EC2 (IaaS): you choose OS and install software. Elastic Beanstalk (PaaS): you upload code, AWS handles servers. Gmail/Salesforce (SaaS): you just use the app.
keyPoints: IaaS: virtual machines, storage, networking; you manage OS, runtime, apps (EC2, EBS, VPC).
PaaS: managed runtime; you manage code and data (Elastic Beanstalk, RDS-style platforms).
SaaS: complete application delivered over the internet (Gmail, Office 365).
Control decreases from IaaS → PaaS → SaaS; convenience increases.
FaaS/serverless (Lambda) is an extension of PaaS.
Responsibility split follows the model.
mustKnow: IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS table.
ifYouKnow: Choose a model for a scenario.
commonMistakes: Calling RDS or Lambda IaaS — they are managed (PaaS-like).
Thinking SaaS needs you to manage servers.

examQuestions.question: IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS.
examQuestions.answer: Compare control, who manages OS/runtime/app, examples.

examQuestions.question: Is AWS Lambda IaaS?
examQuestions.answer: No; it is serverless/FaaS, a managed compute (PaaS-like).

knowledgeCheck.question: In SaaS the user manages the OS.
A team only wants to upload code and not manage servers. Model?

aws-c1-t03.quickRevision: IaaS (EC2) > control; PaaS (Beanstalk) deploy code; SaaS (Gmail) use app.
aws-c1-t03.purpose: Decide how much of the stack the customer vs provider manages.

aws-c1-t04.title: Cloud Deployment Models
aws-c1-t04.definition: Cloud deployment models describe where the cloud infrastructure is hosted and who uses it: public, private, hybrid (and community).
aws-c1-t04.simpleExplanation: Public cloud sabke liye shared (AWS). Private cloud sirf ek organisation ke liye. Hybrid = dono ka mix. Community = kuch similar organisations ka shared.
aws-c1-t04.realLifeAnalogy: Public cloud is a public bus, private cloud is your own car, hybrid is using your car daily and a bus for rush days.
aws-c1-t04.example: A bank keeps sensitive customer data in its private data centre but runs analytics on AWS public cloud, connected by AWS Direct Connect (hybrid).
keyPoints: Public: owned by a provider, shared among customers (AWS, Azure, GCP).
Private: dedicated to one organisation (on-prem or hosted).
Hybrid: public + private connected (e.g. VPN/Direct Connect, AWS Outposts).
Community: shared among organisations with common needs.
Trade-offs: cost, control, compliance, scalability.
AWS also supports 'cloud-native' all-in deployments.
mustKnow: Four models with an example each.
commonMistakes: Thinking private cloud means 'a VPC' — a VPC is private networking inside the public cloud.
Believing hybrid is only for big firms.

examQuestions.question: Public vs private vs hybrid cloud.
examQuestions.answer: Ownership, cost, control, compliance, scalability.

examQuestions.question: Describe hybrid cloud with an example.
examQuestions.answer: On-prem data + AWS compute via Direct Connect.

knowledgeCheck.question: Name a hybrid connectivity service.
knowledgeCheck.answer: AWS Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN.

knowledgeCheck.question: Strict data residency, but needs burst capacity. Model?
Private vs public cost.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Private has higher upfront cost; public is pay-per-use.

aws-c1-t04.purpose: Choose hosting location based on control, compliance and cost.

aws-c1-t05.title: What is AWS?
aws-c1-t05.definition: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is Amazon's cloud platform offering over 200 services for compute, storage, databases, networking, security and more, billed pay-as-you-go.
aws-c1-t05.simpleExplanation: AWS Amazon ka cloud platform hai jaha se tum server, storage, database, AI sab kiraye par le sakte ho. Isko 2006 me launch kiya gaya tha (S3, EC2).
aws-c1-t05.realLifeAnalogy: A huge supermarket of IT building blocks: pick what you need, pay per item used.
aws-c1-t05.example: A student hosts a static website: store files in S3, serve via CloudFront, DNS with Route 53 — all AWS services combined.
keyPoints: Launched publicly in 2006 with S3 and EC2.
Services grouped: compute, storage, database, networking, security, analytics, ML, management.
Pay-as-you-go; Free Tier for beginners.
Accessible via console, CLI, SDKs and APIs.
Shared responsibility model: AWS secures the cloud; customer secures what is in the cloud.
Largest cloud provider by market share (check current reports).
commonMistakes: Thinking AWS is only EC2.
Believing AWS manages your data's security completely.

examQuestions.question: What is AWS? Explain main services.
examQuestions.answer: Definition, categories, examples EC2, S3, RDS, VPC, IAM.

examQuestions.question: Explain the shared responsibility model.
examQuestions.answer: AWS: security OF the cloud; customer: security IN the cloud.

knowledgeCheck.question: Who patches the guest OS of an EC2 instance?
Security OF vs IN the cloud.
knowledgeCheck.answer: OF = AWS hardware/facilities; IN = customer data/config.

aws-c1-t05.quickRevision: AWS: Amazon's cloud (2006), 200+ services, pay-as-you-go, shared responsibility.
aws-c1-t05.purpose: Provide on-demand IT building blocks globally.

aws-c1-t06.title: The AWS Global Infrastructure
aws-c1-t06.definition: The AWS Global Infrastructure is built from Regions, Availability Zones (AZs) and edge locations to provide low latency, high availability and fault tolerance.
aws-c1-t06.simpleExplanation: AWS duniya bhar me Regions me baata hai. Har Region me kai Availability Zones (alag data centres) hote hain. Edge locations content ko users ke paas cache karte hain (CloudFront).
aws-c1-t06.realLifeAnalogy: A courier company with country hubs (Regions), several warehouses in each hub (AZs) and local pickup points (edge locations).
aws-c1-t06.example: An app is deployed in the Mumbai Region across two AZs behind a load balancer; if one AZ fails, traffic goes to the other.
keyPoints: Region: geographic area with multiple AZs (e.g. ap-south-1 Mumbai).
AZ: one or more isolated data centres with separate power/network, connected by low-latency links.
Edge locations/PoPs: used by CloudFront and Route 53 for caching/DNS.
Choose a Region by latency, compliance/data residency, service availability and price.
Multi-AZ deployment gives high availability; multi-Region gives disaster recovery.
Also Local Zones and Wavelength for ultra-low latency.
commonMistakes: Believing an AZ is a single building only — it can be several data centres.
Thinking all services are available in every Region.

examQuestions.question: Explain AWS global infrastructure.
examQuestions.answer: Regions, AZs, edge locations; benefits; Region selection.

examQuestions.question: Region vs AZ.
examQuestions.answer: Region = geography with several AZs; AZ = isolated data-centre group inside a Region.

knowledgeCheck.question: Name one factor for choosing a Region.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Latency, compliance, cost or service availability.

knowledgeCheck.question: Data must stay in India. Choice?
Multi-AZ vs multi-Region.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Multi-AZ = high availability within a Region; multi-Region = disaster recovery across geographies.

aws-c1-t06.quickRevision: Infra: Region ⊃ AZs; edge locations for CloudFront; choose Region by latency/compliance/cost/services.
aws-c1-t06.working: Each Region is isolated; AZs inside it connect by high-speed links; edge locations cache content near users.
aws-c1-t06.scenario: Deploy across 2 AZs; when AZ-a fails, AZ-b serves traffic.

aws-c2-t01.title: Networking Basics
aws-c2-t01.definition: Networking basics cover how devices communicate using IP addresses, CIDR blocks, ports, protocols (TCP/UDP), DNS, routers and switches.
aws-c2-t01.simpleExplanation: Network me har device ka IP address hota hai. CIDR (jaise 10.0.0.0/16) batata hai kitne addresses hain. Ports batate hain kaunsi service (80=HTTP, 443=HTTPS, 22=SSH).
aws-c2-t01.realLifeAnalogy: IP is a house address, port is the room number, router is the post office that decides the route.
keyPoints: IPv4 address = 32 bits; IPv6 = 128 bits.
CIDR /n: first n bits are network; addresses = 2^(32−n).
TCP reliable, connection-oriented; UDP fast, connectionless.
Common ports: 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS, 22 SSH, 3389 RDP, 3306 MySQL.
Router connects networks; switch connects devices in one network.
commonMistakes: Mixing up /16 (large) and /24 (small).
Using public IP ranges in private VPCs.

examQuestions.question: TCP vs UDP.
examQuestions.answer: TCP reliable/ordered; UDP fast/no guarantee.

knowledgeCheck.question: Router vs switch.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Router connects different networks; switch connects devices inside a network.

aws-c2-t01.quickRevision: IP+port; CIDR /n → 2^(32−n) addresses; ports 80/443/22; TCP reliable, UDP fast.

aws-c2-t02.title: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
aws-c2-t02.definition: Amazon VPC is a logically isolated virtual network in an AWS Region where you define the IP range, subnets, routing and security for your resources.
aws-c2-t02.simpleExplanation: VPC AWS cloud me tumhara apna private network hai. Tum IP range, subnets, route tables, gateways aur security khud decide karte ho.
aws-c2-t02.realLifeAnalogy: Your own fenced campus inside a huge city: you decide the buildings (subnets), gates (gateways) and guards (security).
aws-c2-t02.example: Create VPC 10.0.0.0/16 with a public subnet 10.0.1.0/24 (web server) and a private subnet 10.0.2.0/24 (database). Internet gateway attached to the VPC.
keyPoints: Spans all AZs of one Region; subnets are tied to one AZ.
Components: CIDR block, subnets, route tables, Internet Gateway (IGW), NAT gateway, security groups, NACLs, VPC endpoints.
Default VPC exists in each Region for quick start.
VPC peering / Transit Gateway connect VPCs.
VPN or Direct Connect link to on-prem.
Total CIDR size between /16 and /28.
mustKnow: Public vs private subnet in a VPC.
commonMistakes: Thinking a VPC spans Regions (it is Region-scoped).
Forgetting to attach an IGW for internet access.

examQuestions.question: Explain VPC and its components.
examQuestions.answer: CIDR, subnets, route tables, IGW, NAT, SG, NACL.

examQuestions.question: Is a VPC regional or zonal?
examQuestions.answer: Regional; subnets are zonal.

knowledgeCheck.question: A VPC is scoped to a:
What gives a public subnet internet access?
Private DB needs outbound internet for updates. Component?
IGW vs NAT gateway.
knowledgeCheck.answer: IGW gives two-way internet for public resources; NAT gives outbound-only for private resources.

aws-c2-t02.quickRevision: VPC: isolated network per Region; subnets per AZ; IGW, NAT, route tables, SG, NACL.
aws-c2-t02.purpose: Provide isolated, controllable networking for AWS resources.
aws-c2-t02.working: Traffic leaves a subnet by its route table; routes to the IGW make a subnet public; security groups/NACLs filter traffic.
aws-c2-t02.scenario: Web tier in public subnet; database in private subnet reachable only from the web tier.

aws-c2-t03.title: Subnets
aws-c2-t03.definition: A subnet is a range of IP addresses within a VPC located in a single Availability Zone; it is public if its route table sends internet traffic to an Internet Gateway, otherwise private.
aws-c2-t03.simpleExplanation: VPC ko chhote hisson (subnets) me baanta jata hai. Public subnet me internet route hota hai, private me nahi. Har subnet ek AZ me rehta hai.
aws-c2-t03.realLifeAnalogy: Wards of a hospital: reception (public) is open to visitors, ICU (private) is restricted.
aws-c2-t03.example: VPC 10.0.0.0/16 → Public subnet 10.0.1.0/24 in AZ-a (256 addresses, 251 usable). Private subnet 10.0.2.0/24 in AZ-b. AWS reserves 5 IPs per subnet.
keyPoints: Subnet CIDR must be within the VPC CIDR and non-overlapping.
One subnet = one AZ.
AWS reserves 5 addresses per subnet (network, router, DNS, future, broadcast).
Public subnet: route 0.0.0.0/0 → IGW.
Private subnet: no direct internet route.
Use multiple subnets across AZs for high availability.
commonMistakes: Calling a subnet public just because of its name; the route table decides.
Forgetting the 5 reserved IPs.

examQuestions.question: Usable IPs in a /24 AWS subnet?
Public vs private subnet.
examQuestions.answer: Route to IGW vs none.

knowledgeCheck.question: A subnet can span two AZs.
What makes a subnet public?
knowledgeCheck.answer: A route to an Internet Gateway.

knowledgeCheck.question: DB should not be reachable from internet. Subnet?

aws-c2-t03.quickRevision: Subnet: VPC slice in one AZ; public = route to IGW; 5 reserved IPs (251 usable in /24).
aws-c2-t03.purpose: Segment a VPC for security and availability.

aws-c2-t04.title: Route Tables
aws-c2-t04.definition: A route table is a set of rules (routes) that decides where network traffic from a subnet is sent, each route having a destination CIDR and a target.
aws-c2-t04.simpleExplanation: Route table bataata hai ki kisi destination ka traffic kaha bhejna hai. Jaise 0.0.0.0/0 (internet) ko IGW ki taraf bhejna.
aws-c2-t04.realLifeAnalogy: A road signboard at a junction: 'to city X take left'.
aws-c2-t04.example: Public subnet route table: 10.0.0.0/16 → local; 0.0.0.0/0 → igw-123. Private subnet: 10.0.0.0/16 → local; 0.0.0.0/0 → nat-456.
keyPoints: Each VPC has a main route table.
Every route table has a local route for VPC CIDR.
Routes: destination + target (IGW, NAT, peering, VPN, endpoint).
Most specific (longest prefix) route wins.
A subnet is associated with exactly one route table.
Public subnet = route to IGW.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the route to IGW so instances remain unreachable.
Thinking a subnet can have two route tables.

examQuestions.question: Write route tables for public and private subnets.
examQuestions.answer: As in the example.

examQuestions.question: What does 0.0.0.0/0 mean?
examQuestions.answer: All IPv4 destinations (default route).

knowledgeCheck.question: Target for internet in public subnet?
Instance can't reach internet though IGW attached. Check?
Main vs custom route table.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Main is the default for subnets without explicit association; custom is user-created.

aws-c2-t04.quickRevision: Route table: destination→target; local route; 0.0.0.0/0→IGW (public) or NAT (private); longest prefix wins.
aws-c2-t04.working: Packet destination is matched against routes; the most specific match decides the target.

aws-c2-t05.title: Security Groups
aws-c2-t05.definition: A security group is a stateful virtual firewall at the instance (ENI) level that controls inbound and outbound traffic using allow rules.
aws-c2-t05.simpleExplanation: Security group instance ka firewall hai. Isme sirf allow rules hote hain; jo rule allow nahi wo block. Stateful hai: inbound allow hua to uska reply apne aap allow.
aws-c2-t05.realLifeAnalogy: A security guard at a flat's door with a guest list: only listed visitors enter, and anyone you let in can leave without a new pass.
aws-c2-t05.example: Web server SG: inbound TCP 80 from 0.0.0.0/0, TCP 22 from my IP; outbound all. DB SG: inbound 3306 only from the web SG.
keyPoints: Stateful: return traffic automatically allowed.
Allow rules only; no explicit deny.
Default: all inbound denied, all outbound allowed.
Rules reference IPs/CIDRs or other security groups.
Applied to instances/ENIs; many SGs per instance.
Changes apply immediately.
ifYouKnow: Write SG rules for a web + DB tier.
commonMistakes: Trying to create a deny rule in a SG.
Opening SSH 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 unnecessarily.

examQuestions.question: Security group vs NACL.
examQuestions.answer: Instance-level, stateful, allow-only vs subnet-level, stateless, allow+deny with ordered rules.

examQuestions.question: What does stateful mean?
examQuestions.answer: Return traffic of an allowed connection is permitted automatically.

knowledgeCheck.question: Only web servers may reach the DB on 3306. Method?
knowledgeCheck.answer: DB SG allowing source = web SG

knowledgeCheck.question: NACL rule evaluation.
knowledgeCheck.answer: In order by rule number; first match applies.

aws-c2-t05.quickRevision: SG: stateful, instance-level, allow-only, default deny inbound; NACL: stateless, subnet-level, allow+deny.

aws-c2-t06.title: VPC Security
aws-c2-t06.definition: VPC security uses layered controls — security groups, NACLs, private subnets, VPC endpoints, flow logs and IAM — to protect network resources (defence in depth).
aws-c2-t06.simpleExplanation: VPC ko secure karne ke liye kai layers: security groups, NACLs, private subnets, VPC endpoints, flow logs, bastion host. Ek layer fail ho to doosri bachaye.
aws-c2-t06.realLifeAnalogy: A bank with outer gate, ID check, locker and CCTV: many layers.
aws-c2-t06.example: Place web servers in public subnets, app/DB in private subnets, restrict DB SG to the app SG, enable VPC Flow Logs, and use an S3 gateway endpoint so S3 traffic never leaves the AWS network.
keyPoints: Layers: NACL (subnet) + SG (instance).
Put sensitive resources in private subnets.
VPC endpoints give private access to AWS services.
VPC Flow Logs record accepted/rejected traffic.
Bastion host / Systems Manager Session Manager for admin access.
Least privilege with IAM; encryption in transit (TLS).
commonMistakes: Relying on only one control.
Leaving DBs in public subnets.

examQuestions.question: Explain security features of a VPC.
examQuestions.answer: SG, NACL, private subnets, endpoints, flow logs, IAM.

examQuestions.question: Why use a VPC endpoint?
examQuestions.answer: To reach AWS services privately without going over the internet.

knowledgeCheck.question: Need private S3 access from a VPC. Use?
Bastion vs Session Manager.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Bastion is an SSH jump host; Session Manager gives access without opening ports.

aws-c2-t06.quickRevision: VPC security = layers: SG+NACL, private subnets, endpoints, flow logs, bastion/SSM, IAM.

aws-c2-t07.title: DNS: AWS Route 53
aws-c2-t07.definition: Amazon Route 53 is AWS's highly available, scalable DNS service that translates domain names to IP addresses, routes traffic and checks resource health.
aws-c2-t07.simpleExplanation: DNS naam (example.com) ko IP address me badalta hai. Route 53 AWS ka DNS hai (port 53). Ye routing policies aur health checks bhi deta hai.
aws-c2-t07.realLifeAnalogy: The phone book of the internet: you look up a name and get a number.
aws-c2-t07.example: Create a hosted zone for example.com; add an A (alias) record pointing www.example.com to a CloudFront distribution; use weighted routing to send 10% traffic to a new version.
keyPoints: Functions: domain registration, DNS routing, health checking.
Records: A (IPv4), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, alias.
Routing policies: simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation.
Hosted zones: public and private.
Alias records point to AWS resources, work at the zone apex and are free of query charges.
Name '53' from DNS port 53.
commonMistakes: Using CNAME at the zone apex (not allowed).
Confusing DNS (name resolution) with CDN.

examQuestions.question: Explain Route 53 and routing policies.
examQuestions.answer: DNS, health checks, domain registration; simple/weighted/latency/failover/geolocation.

examQuestions.question: Alias vs CNAME.
examQuestions.answer: Alias maps to AWS resources and can be at the apex; CNAME maps names to names and cannot be at apex.

knowledgeCheck.question: Send users to the nearest Region. Policy?
Weighted vs latency routing.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Weighted splits by percentage; latency picks the lowest-latency Region.

aws-c2-t07.quickRevision: Route 53: DNS+health checks+domain registration; A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/alias; policies simple/weighted/latency/failover/geo.
aws-c2-t07.purpose: Resolve domain names and route users reliably.
aws-c2-t07.working: Resolver queries Route 53 name servers; record found; policy picks answer; health checks remove unhealthy targets.
aws-c2-t07.scenario: Failover from primary Region to standby when health check fails.

aws-c2-t08.title: CloudFront
aws-c2-t08.definition: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) that caches content at edge locations to deliver web content to users with low latency.
aws-c2-t08.simpleExplanation: CloudFront ek CDN hai. Content ka copy duniya bhar ke edge locations par cache hota hai, to user ko nazdeeki server se jaldi milta hai.
aws-c2-t08.realLifeAnalogy: A chain of local warehouses stocking popular items so customers don't wait for delivery from the central factory.
aws-c2-t08.example: Static site in S3 (origin) in Mumbai. A user in London requests an image; the nearest edge location serves it from cache; on a miss it fetches from S3 and caches it.
keyPoints: Distribution = CloudFront configuration; origin = S3, ALB, EC2 or custom server.
Edge locations cache based on TTL.
Reduces latency and origin load.
Supports HTTPS, custom domains, WAF and signed URLs.
Origin Access Control restricts S3 to CloudFront only.
Good for static and streaming content.
commonMistakes: Thinking CloudFront stores the only copy; the origin is the source.
Forgetting cache invalidation when content changes.

examQuestions.question: Explain CloudFront.
examQuestions.answer: CDN, edge locations, origin, TTL, benefits.

examQuestions.question: What is a cache miss?
examQuestions.answer: Edge does not have the object, so it fetches it from the origin.

knowledgeCheck.question: CloudFront can use S3 as origin.
Benefit of CDN?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Lower latency and reduced origin load.

knowledgeCheck.question: Updated image not showing. Fix?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Invalidate the cache or lower TTL.

knowledgeCheck.question: Route 53 vs CloudFront.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Route 53 resolves names; CloudFront delivers cached content.

aws-c2-t08.quickRevision: CloudFront: CDN; edge caching; origin (S3/ALB); TTL; HTTPS; invalidation.
aws-c2-t08.purpose: Deliver content globally with low latency.
aws-c2-t08.working: User → nearest edge; hit → serve from cache; miss → fetch from origin, cache, serve.
aws-c2-t08.scenario: Global users loading images from an S3 bucket via CloudFront.

aws-c2-t09.title: Build Your VPC in AWS and Launch a Web Server
aws-c2-t09.definition: Building a VPC and launching a web server means creating a VPC with a public subnet, internet gateway, route table and security group, and starting an EC2 instance running a web server.
aws-c2-t09.simpleExplanation: Lab steps: VPC banao, public subnet banao, IGW attach karo, route table me 0.0.0.0/0→IGW daalo, security group me port 80 kholo, EC2 launch karo aur user data se web server install karo.
aws-c2-t09.realLifeAnalogy: Building a small shop: plot (VPC), road to the highway (IGW + route), shop (EC2), and a door policy (security group).
aws-c2-t09.example: VPC 10.0.0.0/16; public subnet 10.0.1.0/24; IGW attached; route 0.0.0.0/0→IGW; SG allow TCP 80 (anywhere) and 22 (my IP); EC2 (Amazon Linux) with user data below; open http://<public-IP>.
keyPoints: Create VPC with CIDR.
Create public subnet in an AZ; enable auto-assign public IPv4.
Create and attach Internet Gateway.
Route table: add 0.0.0.0/0 → IGW; associate with subnet.
Security group: inbound 80 and 22.

aws-c3-t01.title: IaaS
aws-c3-t01.definition: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) provides virtualised computing resources such as servers, storage and networking on demand, while the customer manages the OS, middleware and applications.
aws-c3-t01.simpleExplanation: IaaS me AWS hardware, network aur virtualisation sambhalta hai; tum OS, software aur app sambhalte ho. Sabse zyada control, sabse zyada zimmedari.
aws-c3-t01.realLifeAnalogy: Renting an empty flat: the building is maintained for you, but furnishing and running it is your job.
aws-c3-t01.example: Launch an EC2 instance, install Apache and your app yourself, attach EBS volumes and place it in a VPC — all IaaS building blocks.
keyPoints: AWS IaaS services: EC2, EBS, VPC, ELB.
Customer manages OS patching, runtime and applications.
Provider manages data centres, hardware and hypervisor.
Highest flexibility among service models.
Pay for what you provision.
Suitable for lift-and-shift migration.
commonMistakes: Thinking IaaS includes OS patching by AWS.
Calling Lambda IaaS.

examQuestions.question: Define IaaS with AWS examples.
examQuestions.answer: Virtualised infrastructure on demand; EC2, EBS, VPC.

examQuestions.question: Who patches the OS on EC2?
examQuestions.answer: The customer.

knowledgeCheck.question: In IaaS the customer manages the OS.
Need a custom OS configuration. Model?
IaaS vs PaaS control.
knowledgeCheck.answer: IaaS gives more control; PaaS manages OS/runtime.

aws-c3-t01.quickRevision: IaaS = virtual servers/storage/network on demand; you manage OS+apps (EC2).
aws-c3-t01.purpose: Rent infrastructure instead of owning it.

aws-c3-t02.title: Virtual Machines in the Cloud
aws-c3-t02.definition: A virtual machine (VM) is a software-emulated computer running on shared physical hardware via a hypervisor, with its own OS and resources.
aws-c3-t02.simpleExplanation: Ek physical server par hypervisor kai VMs chalata hai; har VM apna alag computer jaisa behave karta hai. EC2 instances VMs hi hain (Nitro hypervisor).
aws-c3-t02.realLifeAnalogy: One big building (physical server) divided into separate apartments (VMs), each with its own door and utilities.
aws-c3-t02.example: One physical server hosts 10 EC2 instances of different customers, each isolated, with its own OS and IP.
keyPoints: Hypervisor virtualises CPU, memory, storage and network.
AWS uses the Nitro system for EC2.
VMs boot from an AMI (image).
Multi-tenancy with isolation.
VM vs container: VM has full OS; container shares host kernel and is lighter.
Benefits: better utilisation, quick provisioning, snapshots.
commonMistakes: Thinking a VM is a physical server.
Confusing VM with container.

examQuestions.question: Explain virtual machines in the cloud.
examQuestions.answer: Hypervisor, isolation, AMI, EC2.

examQuestions.question: VM vs container.
examQuestions.answer: VM includes guest OS (heavier); container shares host OS kernel (lighter).

knowledgeCheck.question: What is an AMI?
knowledgeCheck.answer: A template with OS and software used to launch an instance.

knowledgeCheck.question: Many isolated servers on one host. Technology?
VM vs bare metal.
knowledgeCheck.answer: VM shares hardware via hypervisor; bare metal gives direct hardware.

aws-c3-t02.quickRevision: VM = software computer on shared hardware via hypervisor; EC2 (Nitro); AMI boots it.
aws-c3-t02.purpose: Use hardware efficiently and provision servers quickly.
aws-c3-t02.working: Hypervisor splits host resources among isolated VMs, each booted from an image.

aws-c3-t03.title: Amazon EC2
aws-c3-t03.definition: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) provides resizable virtual servers (instances) in the cloud that you launch from an AMI and configure with instance type, storage and security.
aws-c3-t03.simpleExplanation: EC2 AWS ka virtual server hai. Tum AMI chunte ho, instance type (CPU/RAM) chunte ho, key pair aur security group lagate ho, aur server tayyar.
aws-c3-t03.realLifeAnalogy: Renting a computer by the hour, choosing the size you need and returning it when done.
aws-c3-t03.example: Run a web app on a t3.micro instance (Linux AMI), attach a 20 GB EBS volume and a security group that allows HTTP. Later resize to t3.medium when traffic grows.
keyPoints: Instance families: general purpose (t, m), compute optimised (c), memory optimised (r), storage optimised (i), accelerated (p, g).
Needs: AMI, instance type, key pair, network/security group, storage (EBS or instance store).
Purchasing: On-Demand, Reserved/Savings Plans, Spot, Dedicated Hosts.
Instance states: pending, running, stopping, stopped, terminated.
Instance store is temporary; EBS persists.
Billed per second (Linux) while running.
commonMistakes: Thinking stopped instances still pay compute charges (EBS still billed).
Using Spot for critical non-interruptible jobs.

examQuestions.question: Explain EC2 features and purchasing options.
examQuestions.answer: Families, AMI, key pair, SG, EBS; On-Demand, Reserved, Spot, Dedicated.

examQuestions.question: On-Demand vs Spot.
examQuestions.answer: On-Demand: pay normal rate, no interruption; Spot: spare capacity at big discount but can be reclaimed.

knowledgeCheck.question: Stop vs terminate.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Stop keeps the instance and EBS; terminate deletes the instance.

aws-c3-t03.quickRevision: EC2 = resizable VMs: AMI + type + key pair + SG + EBS; On-Demand/Reserved/Spot/Dedicated.

aws-c3-t04.title: Elastic Load Balancing
aws-c3-t04.definition: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) automatically distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets such as EC2 instances in one or more Availability Zones.
aws-c3-t04.simpleExplanation: Load balancer traffic ko kai servers me baant deta hai taki koi ek server overload na ho. Health check se kharab server ko traffic nahi bhejta.
aws-c3-t04.realLifeAnalogy: A traffic police officer directing cars to different lanes so no lane jams.
aws-c3-t04.example: Two EC2 web servers in different AZs behind an Application Load Balancer; if one fails its health check, ALB sends all requests to the healthy one.
keyPoints: Types: Application (L7, HTTP/HTTPS, path/host routing), Network (L4, TCP/UDP, high performance, static IP), Gateway (L3, appliances), Classic (legacy).
Target group: set of targets with health checks.
Listeners and rules define routing.
Cross-zone load balancing spreads evenly across AZs.
Supports SSL termination.
Gives high availability and fault tolerance.
commonMistakes: Using NLB when you need path-based routing (that's ALB).
Putting all targets in a single AZ.

examQuestions.question: ALB vs NLB.
examQuestions.answer: ALB: layer 7, content routing; NLB: layer 4, ultra-high performance.

examQuestions.question: Explain ELB and its benefits.
examQuestions.answer: Distribute traffic, health checks, multi-AZ, scalable.

knowledgeCheck.question: Path-based routing is a feature of:
ELB vs Route 53.
knowledgeCheck.answer: ELB balances among instances; Route 53 resolves DNS and routes at DNS level.

aws-c3-t04.quickRevision: ELB: ALB (L7, path/host), NLB (L4, fast), GLB (L3); target groups + health checks; multi-AZ.
aws-c3-t04.working: Client → listener rule → healthy target in a target group.

aws-c3-t05.title: AutoScaling
aws-c3-t05.definition: EC2 Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to match demand and maintain a desired number of healthy instances.
aws-c3-t05.simpleExplanation: Auto Scaling traffic badhne par naye servers add karta hai aur kam hone par hata deta hai. Kharab instance ko replace bhi karta hai.
aws-c3-t05.realLifeAnalogy: A restaurant calling extra waiters when it gets crowded and sending them home when it's quiet.
aws-c3-t05.example: ASG min=2, desired=2, max=6 with a target-tracking policy: keep average CPU at 50%. During a sale CPU hits 80% → ASG launches more instances up to 6.
keyPoints: Auto Scaling group (ASG): min, desired, max capacity.
Launch template defines AMI, type, SG, key.
Policies: target tracking, step, scheduled, predictive.
Health checks replace unhealthy instances.
Works with ELB across AZs.
Improves cost and availability.
commonMistakes: Confusing scaling out (add instances) with scaling up (bigger instance).
Setting min=0 for a critical service.

examQuestions.question: Explain Auto Scaling with policies.
examQuestions.answer: ASG, launch template, policies, health checks.

examQuestions.question: Scale out vs scale up.
examQuestions.answer: Out: more instances (horizontal); up: larger instance (vertical).

knowledgeCheck.question: Traffic spike every day at 9 am. Policy?
Horizontal vs vertical scaling.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Horizontal adds instances; vertical increases instance size.

aws-c3-t05.quickRevision: ASG: launch template + min/desired/max + policies (target/step/scheduled) + health checks; with ELB.

aws-c3-t06.title: Launch an Amazon EC2 Instance
aws-c3-t06.definition: Launching an EC2 instance means choosing an AMI, instance type, key pair, network and storage settings in the console or CLI and starting the server.
aws-c3-t06.simpleExplanation: Console me: Launch instance → naam → AMI (Amazon Linux) → type (t3.micro) → key pair → security group → storage → Launch. Phir SSH se connect.
aws-c3-t06.realLifeAnalogy: Booking a hotel room: choose room type, give an ID, get a key, enter.
aws-c3-t06.example: Launch Amazon Linux t3.micro, key pair mykey, SG allowing SSH 22 from your IP. Connect: ssh -i mykey.pem ec2-user@<public-ip>.
keyPoints: Steps: name → AMI → instance type → key pair → network/SG → storage → advanced (user data) → Launch.
Key pair file (.pem) needed for SSH; keep it private (chmod 400).
Security group must allow SSH (22) or RDP (3389).
Free Tier eligible types for learning.
Terminate when done to avoid charges.
Check instance status checks (2/2 passed).

Missing SSH rule in the SG.
Forgetting to terminate.

aws-c3-t07.title: Serverless Computing
aws-c3-t07.definition: Serverless computing lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers; the provider scales automatically and you pay only for execution.
aws-c3-t07.simpleExplanation: Serverless me server hote to hain par tum unhe manage nahi karte. Code likho, AWS chalaata hai, scale karta hai, aur sirf run time ka paisa lagta hai.
aws-c3-t07.realLifeAnalogy: Taking a cab instead of owning a car: you pay per ride and never worry about maintenance.
aws-c3-t07.example: An image uploaded to S3 triggers a Lambda function that creates a thumbnail and stores it back. No server is running when nothing is uploaded.
keyPoints: No server management; automatic scaling.
Pay per request/duration; zero cost when idle.
Event-driven.
AWS serverless: Lambda, Fargate, API Gateway, DynamoDB, S3, SQS/SNS.
Limits: cold starts, execution time caps, vendor lock-in.
Good for variable, event-driven workloads.
commonMistakes: Thinking 'serverless' means no servers exist.
Using it for long-running jobs.

examQuestions.question: Explain serverless computing and benefits.
examQuestions.answer: No server management, auto-scale, pay-per-use, event-driven.

examQuestions.question: Drawback of serverless?
examQuestions.answer: Cold starts, time limits, lock-in.

knowledgeCheck.question: You pay when a serverless function is idle.

aws-c3-t07.quickRevision: Serverless: no servers to manage, auto-scale, pay per use, event-driven (Lambda, Fargate).

aws-c3-t08.title: AWS Lambda
aws-c3-t08.definition: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs your function in response to events and charges only for the compute time used.
aws-c3-t08.simpleExplanation: Lambda me tum function likhte ho; koi event (S3 upload, API call, schedule) aaye to AWS use chalata hai. Server ki chinta nahi.
aws-c3-t08.realLifeAnalogy: A vending machine: it does its job when someone presses a button, and costs nothing otherwise.
aws-c3-t08.example: Python handler: def lambda_handler(event, context): name=event.get('name','World'); return {'statusCode':200,'body':f'Hello {name}'}. Triggered through API Gateway.
keyPoints: Function + trigger + execution role.
Triggers: S3, API Gateway, DynamoDB streams, SQS, EventBridge schedules.
Runtimes: Python, Node.js, Java, .NET, Go, Ruby, custom/container.
Timeout up to 15 minutes; memory 128 MB–10,240 MB.
Billed on requests and duration (GB-seconds).
Scales automatically per request.
commonMistakes: Using Lambda for jobs longer than 15 minutes.
Forgetting the execution role permissions.

examQuestions.question: Explain AWS Lambda with example.
examQuestions.answer: Event-driven functions; S3 thumbnail example.

examQuestions.question: Lambda max timeout?
examQuestions.answer: 15 minutes.

knowledgeCheck.question: Lambda needs you to manage servers.
Lambda vs EC2 billing.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Lambda per request/duration; EC2 per running time.

aws-c3-t08.quickRevision: Lambda: event→function (≤15 min), pay per request+duration, triggers S3/API GW/EventBridge, execution role.
aws-c3-t08.purpose: Run code on events without servers.
aws-c3-t08.working: Event arrives → Lambda starts execution environment → runs handler → returns result; scales per concurrent event.

aws-c3-t09.title: Characteristics of AWS Lambda
aws-c3-t09.definition: The characteristics of Lambda are event-driven execution, stateless functions, automatic scaling, pay-per-use billing, managed runtimes and defined resource limits.
aws-c3-t09.simpleExplanation: Lambda ki khaas baatein: event se chalta hai, stateless hai, khud scale hota hai, sirf use ka paisa, aur kuch limits (time, memory) hote hain.
aws-c3-t09.realLifeAnalogy: A temporary worker called per task who forgets everything after the job, so any notes must go to a shared notebook (S3/DynamoDB).
aws-c3-t09.example: A function counting visits can't keep a counter in memory between calls; it stores the count in DynamoDB.
keyPoints: Event-driven and stateless; persist data externally.
Automatic scaling and high availability across AZs.
Pay per request and duration in milliseconds.
Limits: 15 min timeout, up to 10 GB memory, /tmp storage, package size limits.
Cold start delay on first/new execution environment.
Concurrency limits; reserved/provisioned concurrency options.
Security via execution role and resource policies.
commonMistakes: Storing state in function memory expecting persistence.
Ignoring concurrency limits.

examQuestions.question: List characteristics of AWS Lambda.
examQuestions.answer: Event-driven, stateless, auto-scale, pay-per-use, limits.

aws-c3-t10.title: Create and Configure a Lambda Function
aws-c3-t10.definition: Creating a Lambda function involves choosing a runtime, writing a handler, setting an execution role, configuring memory, timeout and triggers, and testing with an event.

Too small timeout for slow code.

aws-c3-t11.title: PaaS: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
aws-c3-t11.definition: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS that deploys and manages web applications by automatically provisioning EC2, load balancing, Auto Scaling and monitoring from your uploaded code.
aws-c3-t11.simpleExplanation: Beanstalk me bas code upload karo; AWS EC2, load balancer, auto scaling aur monitoring khud set up kar deta hai. Tum control rakh sakte ho par infra ka kaam kam.
aws-c3-t11.realLifeAnalogy: Moving into a furnished serviced apartment: you bring your belongings (code); setup and maintenance are handled.
aws-c3-t11.example: Upload a Python Flask app zip; Beanstalk creates an environment with EC2 + ALB + Auto Scaling and gives a URL.
keyPoints: Supports Java, .NET, PHP, Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, Docker.
Environment types: web server and worker.
Deployment policies: all at once, rolling, rolling with additional batch, immutable, blue/green.
No extra charge; you pay for underlying resources.
You retain access to the underlying resources.
Monitoring via CloudWatch and health dashboard.
commonMistakes: Thinking Beanstalk removes all control; you can customise.
Confusing with CloudFormation (infrastructure templates).

aws-c4-t01.title: Object Storage, Block Storage, and File Storage
aws-c4-t01.definition: Object storage stores data as objects with metadata and keys (S3), block storage stores data in fixed blocks attached to a server like a disk (EBS), and file storage provides a shared file system (EFS).
aws-c4-t01.simpleExplanation: Object = files ko key se store karna (S3). Block = disk jaisa, ek server se attach (EBS). File = shared folder jise kai servers use karein (EFS).
aws-c4-t01.realLifeAnalogy: Object storage is a warehouse with labelled boxes, block storage is your laptop's hard disk, file storage is a shared network drive.
aws-c4-t01.example: Photos and backups in S3; the OS and database disk on EBS; shared web content for many servers on EFS.
keyPoints: Object: flat namespace, bucket+key, metadata, HTTP access, unlimited scale (S3).
Block: raw volume formatted with a file system, low latency, one instance at a time (EBS).
File: hierarchical shared files via NFS, many instances (EFS).
Choose by access pattern and latency.

Durability/cost differ.

aws-c4-t02.title: AWS Storage Services: Amazon S3
aws-c4-t02.definition: Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) is a highly durable, scalable object storage service that stores objects in buckets.
aws-c4-t02.simpleExplanation: S3 me files (objects) buckets me rakhte hain. Har object ki ek key hoti hai. Ye bahut durable hai (11 nines) aur lagbhag unlimited store kar sakta hai.

keyPoints: Bucket names are globally unique; buckets live in a Region.
Object = data + key + metadata; max object size 5 TB.
Durability 99.999999999% (11 nines).
Features: versioning, lifecycle rules, encryption, replication, access policies.
Strong read-after-write consistency.

Making buckets public accidentally.

examQuestions.question: Explain Amazon S3 features.

knowledgeCheck.question: Bucket vs object.

aws-c4-t02.quickRevision: S3: buckets+objects, 11 nines durability, versioning/lifecycle/encryption, 5 TB object max.

aws-c4-t03.title: Various Storage Classes of S3
aws-c4-t03.definition: S3 storage classes offer different cost/availability/retrieval trade-offs, from S3 Standard for frequent access to Glacier Deep Archive for long-term archives.
aws-c4-t03.simpleExplanation: S3 ke alag-alag classes hain: jitna kam access, utna sasta storage par retrieval slow/costly. Lifecycle policy se data apne aap sasti class me chala jaata hai.
aws-c4-t03.realLifeAnalogy: A house: everyday items in the living room (Standard), seasonal items in the store room (IA), old records in the attic (Glacier).
aws-c4-t03.example: Logs: first 30 days S3 Standard → move to Standard-IA → after 90 days Glacier Flexible Retrieval → after a year Glacier Deep Archive using lifecycle rules.
keyPoints: Standard: frequent access, low latency.
Intelligent-Tiering: auto moves between tiers.
Standard-IA: infrequent access, retrieval fee, min 30 days.
One Zone-IA: single AZ, cheaper, less resilient.
Glacier Instant Retrieval; Glacier Flexible Retrieval (minutes–hours); Glacier Deep Archive (cheapest, hours).

ifYouKnow: Choose a class for a use case.
commonMistakes: Using One Zone-IA for critical data.
Ignoring retrieval charges and minimum duration.

examQuestions.question: Explain S3 storage classes.
examQuestions.answer: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier tiers.

examQuestions.question: Which class is cheapest for archives?
examQuestions.answer: Glacier Deep Archive.

knowledgeCheck.question: One Zone-IA stores data in one AZ.
What moves objects between classes automatically?
Standard vs Standard-IA.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Standard: no retrieval fee, higher storage price; IA: lower storage, retrieval fee.

aws-c4-t03.quickRevision: S3 classes: Standard → Int-Tiering → Standard-IA → One Zone-IA → Glacier IR/Flexible/Deep Archive; lifecycle automates moves.
aws-c4-t03.purpose: Optimise storage cost by access pattern.

aws-c4-t04.title: Amazon EFS
aws-c4-t04.definition: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) is a fully managed, elastic, shared NFS file system for Linux workloads that can be mounted by many EC2 instances across AZs.
aws-c4-t04.simpleExplanation: EFS ek shared network folder hai jo apne aap bada-chhota hota hai. Kai EC2 servers ek saath mount kar sakte hain (Linux, NFS).
aws-c4-t04.realLifeAnalogy: A shared office drive that automatically grows as people add files.
aws-c4-t04.example: Three web servers in different AZs mount /mnt/efs to serve the same uploaded images.
keyPoints: Managed NFS (v4) file system; POSIX-compliant.
Elastic: grows/shrinks automatically; pay for storage used.
Multi-AZ, accessible by thousands of instances concurrently.
Linux only (not Windows).
Storage classes: Standard and Infrequent Access (lifecycle).
Mount targets in each AZ.
commonMistakes: Trying to mount EFS on Windows.
Using EFS where a single-instance disk (EBS) is enough.

examQuestions.question: EFS vs EBS.
examQuestions.answer: EFS shared multi-AZ NFS elastic; EBS single-AZ block volume for one instance.

examQuestions.question: Protocol used by EFS?
examQuestions.answer: NFS.

knowledgeCheck.question: EFS can be mounted by many instances.
Shared content across web servers. Service?
EFS vs S3.
knowledgeCheck.answer: EFS is a file system; S3 is object storage over HTTP.

aws-c4-t04.quickRevision: EFS: managed elastic NFS, multi-AZ, shared by many Linux instances.
aws-c4-t04.working: Create EFS → create mount targets → mount on instances with NFS.

aws-c4-t05.title: Amazon EBS
aws-c4-t05.definition: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) provides persistent block storage volumes for EC2 instances, living in a single Availability Zone.
aws-c4-t05.simpleExplanation: EBS EC2 ka hard disk hai jo instance band hone par bhi data rakhta hai. Ek AZ me hota hai aur snapshot se backup hota hai.
aws-c4-t05.realLifeAnalogy: An external hard disk plugged into a computer: data stays even if the computer is switched off.
aws-c4-t05.example: Attach a 100 GB gp3 volume to a database server; take daily snapshots stored in S3.
keyPoints: Volume types: gp3/gp2 (SSD general), io2/io1 (provisioned IOPS), st1 (throughput HDD), sc1 (cold HDD).
Tied to one AZ; attach to instances in the same AZ.
Snapshots stored in S3, incremental; can copy across Regions.
Supports encryption.
Persistent, unlike instance store.
Can resize and change type online.
commonMistakes: Attaching a volume to an instance in another AZ.
Assuming instance store persists.

examQuestions.question: Explain EBS volume types and snapshots.
examQuestions.answer: Types; snapshots incremental to S3.

examQuestions.question: EBS vs instance store.
examQuestions.answer: EBS persistent network volume; instance store temporary and local.

knowledgeCheck.question: EBS volume is tied to one AZ.
Move volume to another AZ. How?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Snapshot → create volume in target AZ.

knowledgeCheck.question: gp3 vs io2.
knowledgeCheck.answer: gp3 general purpose; io2 provisioned high IOPS.

aws-c4-t05.quickRevision: EBS: persistent block volumes, one AZ, gp3/io2/st1/sc1, snapshots → S3.
aws-c4-t05.working: Create volume in AZ → attach to instance → format and mount → snapshot for backup.

aws-c4-t06.title: Create an Amazon EBS Volume
aws-c4-t06.definition: Creating an EBS volume means creating it in the same AZ as the instance, attaching it, then formatting and mounting it inside the OS.
aws-c4-t06.simpleExplanation: Steps: EC2 → Volumes → Create volume (type, size, same AZ) → Attach to instance → instance me format (mkfs) aur mount karo.
aws-c4-t06.realLifeAnalogy: Buying a new hard disk, plugging it in, formatting and giving it a drive letter.
aws-c4-t06.example: Create 10 GB gp3 in ap-south-1a; attach as /dev/sdf; on Linux run lsblk, mkfs, mount to /data.
keyPoints: Create in the same AZ as the instance.
Choose type (gp3), size, optional encryption.
Attach to the instance with a device name.
Inside the OS: find the device (lsblk), format (mkfs), mount.
Add to /etc/fstab for auto-mount.
Snapshot for backup; delete when not needed.
commonMistakes: Creating the volume in a different AZ.
Formatting an existing volume that has data.

examQuestions.question: Steps to create and attach an EBS volume.
examQuestions.answer: As listed.

examQuestions.question: Why can't I see the new disk space?
examQuestions.answer: It must be formatted and mounted in the OS.

knowledgeCheck.question: Volume and instance must be in the same AZ.
Data lost after reboot of mount. Fix?
Snapshot vs AMI.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Snapshot backs up a volume; AMI is a full image (volume snapshots + metadata).

aws-c4-t06.quickRevision: EBS lab: create (same AZ) → attach → lsblk → mkfs → mount → fstab → snapshot.
aws-c4-t06.working: Console: EC2 → Volumes → Create → Attach. OS: format and mount.
aws-c4-t06.code:
lsblk
sudo mkfs -t xfs /dev/xvdf
sudo mkdir /data

df -h

aws-c4-t07.title: Hosting a Static Website using S3
aws-c4-t07.definition: S3 static website hosting serves HTML, CSS, JS and images directly from a bucket using the S3 website endpoint, with a public-read policy or CloudFront.
aws-c4-t07.simpleExplanation: Static website me sirf HTML/CSS/JS hota hai. S3 bucket me files daalo, static website hosting ON karo, public read allow karo, aur website endpoint kholo.
aws-c4-t07.realLifeAnalogy: Pinning a printed poster on a public notice board that anyone can read.
aws-c4-t07.example: Bucket my-site-demo: upload index.html and error.html; enable static website hosting with index.html as index; add a bucket policy allowing s3:GetObject; open http://my-site-demo.s3-website-<region>.amazonaws.com.
keyPoints: Create a bucket (name globally unique).
Upload index.html and error.html.
Enable Static website hosting; set index and error documents.
Allow public read: turn off Block Public Access + bucket policy.
Access through the S3 website endpoint (HTTP).
For HTTPS and custom domain use CloudFront + Route 53.
commonMistakes: Leaving Block Public Access on and getting 403.
Expecting HTTPS on the S3 website endpoint.

examQuestions.question: Steps to host a static website on S3.
examQuestions.answer: As listed.

examQuestions.question: Why 403 Forbidden?
examQuestions.answer: Public access blocked or missing GetObject policy.

knowledgeCheck.question: Static sites can run server-side PHP on S3.
S3 hosting vs EC2 hosting.
knowledgeCheck.answer: S3: static only, cheap, no servers; EC2: dynamic apps, you manage servers.

aws-c4-t07.quickRevision: S3 static site: bucket → upload → enable hosting → public GetObject policy → endpoint; HTTPS via CloudFront.
aws-c4-t07.working: Enable website hosting and public read; browsers fetch objects through the website endpoint.

aws-c5-t01.title: AWS Well-Architected Framework Design Principles
aws-c5-t01.definition: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is a set of best practices organised into six pillars — operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimisation and sustainability — for designing good cloud architectures.
aws-c5-t01.simpleExplanation: Well-Architected Framework batata hai achha cloud design kaisa hota hai. 6 pillars hain: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.
aws-c5-t01.realLifeAnalogy: A building checklist: strong foundation (reliability), locks (security), smooth operations, efficiency, budget control and eco-friendliness.
aws-c5-t01.example: Review a web app: Multi-AZ + Auto Scaling (reliability), IAM least privilege (security), CloudWatch alarms (operations), right-sized instances (cost/performance).
keyPoints: Operational Excellence: automate, small reversible changes, learn from failures.
Security: least privilege, protect data, traceability.
Reliability: recover from failure, scale horizontally, stop guessing capacity.
Performance Efficiency: right resource types, serverless, experiment.
Cost Optimization: pay for what you use, measure, avoid waste.
Sustainability: reduce environmental impact.
General principles: automate, test at scale, data-driven design, game days.
mustKnow: Six pillars with one principle each.
commonMistakes: Forgetting sustainability (added 2021).
Treating cost optimisation as 'cheapest option' only.

examQuestions.question: Explain the AWS Well-Architected Framework pillars.
examQuestions.answer: List and explain six pillars with examples.

examQuestions.question: Which pillar covers multi-AZ design?
examQuestions.answer: Reliability.

knowledgeCheck.question: Using Auto Scaling instead of guessing capacity. Pillar?
Reliability vs Performance Efficiency.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Reliability = recover and stay available; performance = use resources efficiently.

aws-c5-t01.quickRevision: Six pillars: Ops Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.

aws-c5-t02.title: Relational Database Service
aws-c5-t02.definition: A relational database stores structured data in tables with rows and columns, uses SQL and provides ACID transactions; a relational database service provides this as a managed offering.
aws-c5-t02.simpleExplanation: Relational database me data tables me hota hai (rows, columns), tables relations se jude hote hain, SQL se query karte hain. Managed service me AWS admin ka kaam sambhalta hai.
aws-c5-t02.realLifeAnalogy: A set of linked Excel sheets with strict column rules and formulas that keep data consistent.
aws-c5-t02.example: Students table (id, name) and Marks table (student_id, subject, marks). JOIN gives each student's marks. A bank transfer must be ACID: both debit and credit succeed or both fail.
keyPoints: Tables, rows, columns, primary key, foreign key.
SQL for queries.
ACID: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.
Good for structured, transactional (OLTP) workloads.
Managed vs self-managed (EC2): patching, backups, HA handled by service.
AWS options: RDS, Aurora.
commonMistakes: Thinking relational means no scaling; it scales with replicas/Aurora.
Confusing ACID with BASE.

examQuestions.question: What is a relational database service?
examQuestions.answer: Structured tables, SQL, ACID, managed by AWS.

examQuestions.question: Relational vs NoSQL.
examQuestions.answer: Schema/tables/SQL/ACID vs flexible schema/key-value/scale-out.

knowledgeCheck.question: RDS vs DB on EC2.
knowledgeCheck.answer: RDS is managed; DB on EC2 is self-managed.

aws-c5-t02.quickRevision: Relational = tables+SQL+ACID; managed service handles backup/patch/HA (RDS/Aurora).

aws-c5-t03.title: MySQL
aws-c5-t03.definition: MySQL is a popular open-source relational database engine supported by Amazon RDS and Aurora.
aws-c5-t03.simpleExplanation: MySQL ek open-source relational database hai, web apps me bahut use hota hai. RDS me MySQL ko managed tareeke se chala sakte ho (port 3306).
aws-c5-t03.realLifeAnalogy: A well-known, reliable filing cabinet that most small web apps already know how to use.
aws-c5-t03.example: CREATE TABLE student(id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(50)); INSERT INTO student VALUES (1,'Asha'); SELECT * FROM student; Output: 1 | Asha.
keyPoints: Open source (owned by Oracle).
Default port 3306.
ACID with InnoDB engine.
Used in LAMP/WordPress stacks.
RDS offers MySQL with Multi-AZ, backups, read replicas.
Aurora MySQL-compatible is faster and more scalable.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to open port 3306 in the SG.
Assuming MyISAM is transactional.

examQuestions.question: Create and query a table in MySQL.
examQuestions.answer: CREATE, INSERT, SELECT example.

knowledgeCheck.question: MySQL vs PostgreSQL.
knowledgeCheck.answer: MySQL simpler/popular for web; PostgreSQL more advanced features.

aws-c5-t03.quickRevision: MySQL: open-source RDBMS, port 3306, InnoDB ACID; RDS/Aurora support.

aws-c5-t04.title: PostgreSQL
aws-c5-t04.definition: PostgreSQL is an advanced open-source object-relational database known for standards compliance, extensibility and rich data types such as JSONB.
aws-c5-t04.simpleExplanation: PostgreSQL ek powerful open-source database hai: complex queries, JSON, extensions, strict standards. RDS aur Aurora dono support karte hain (port 5432).
aws-c5-t04.realLifeAnalogy: A Swiss-army knife database with extra tools for complex jobs.
aws-c5-t04.example: CREATE TABLE product(id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, data JSONB); INSERT INTO product(data) VALUES ('{"name":"pen"}'); SELECT data->>'name' FROM product; Output: pen.
keyPoints: Default port 5432.
Supports JSONB, arrays, custom types, window functions.
Extensions such as PostGIS.
Strong ACID and MVCC.
Available on RDS and Aurora PostgreSQL.
Good for complex analytical and geospatial queries.
commonMistakes: Mixing port numbers (5432 vs 3306).
Thinking PostgreSQL has no JSON.

examQuestions.question: PostgreSQL vs MySQL.
examQuestions.answer: PostgreSQL: richer features, extensions, strict standards; MySQL: simpler, popular for web.

knowledgeCheck.question: Need advanced JSON and geospatial queries. Engine?
PostgreSQL vs SQL Server licensing.
knowledgeCheck.answer: PostgreSQL is open source; SQL Server is commercial.

aws-c5-t04.quickRevision: PostgreSQL: open-source object-relational, port 5432, JSONB, extensions (PostGIS).

aws-c5-t05.title: SQL Server
aws-c5-t05.definition: Microsoft SQL Server is a commercial relational database that Amazon RDS supports with License Included or bring-your-own-license options.
aws-c5-t05.simpleExplanation: SQL Server Microsoft ka commercial database hai (T-SQL, port 1433). RDS me 'License Included' ke saath chala sakte ho, jisme license ka cost bill me hota hai.
aws-c5-t05.realLifeAnalogy: A corporate-grade database from the Microsoft ecosystem, usually chosen when the company already uses Windows tools.
aws-c5-t05.example: SELECT TOP 5 name FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC; — T-SQL query to get top 5 students.
keyPoints: Default port 1433.
Query language: T-SQL.
Editions: Express, Web, Standard, Enterprise.
Integrates with .NET, Active Directory.
RDS provides backups, Multi-AZ and patching.
Higher cost due to licensing.
commonMistakes: Forgetting licensing costs.
Mixing LIMIT (MySQL) with TOP (T-SQL).

examQuestions.question: Explain SQL Server on RDS.
examQuestions.answer: T-SQL, port 1433, editions, license included, managed features.

examQuestions.question: SQL Server query language?
examQuestions.answer: T-SQL.

knowledgeCheck.question: RDS SQL Server may include the license.
SQL Server vs MySQL cost.
knowledgeCheck.answer: SQL Server has licence costs; MySQL is open source.

aws-c5-t05.quickRevision: SQL Server: Microsoft, T-SQL, port 1433, editions, RDS license included.
aws-c5-t05.purpose: Commercial relational engine for Microsoft stacks.
aws-c5-t05.code: SELECT TOP 5 name FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC;

aws-c5-t06.title: Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service)
aws-c5-t06.definition: Amazon RDS is a managed service that sets up, operates and scales relational databases, handling backups, patching, monitoring and high availability.
aws-c5-t06.simpleExplanation: RDS me database server tumhe nahi sambhalna: AWS backup, patching, failover sambhalta hai. Engines: Aurora, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server.
aws-c5-t06.realLifeAnalogy: Hiring a facility manager for your database: you use it, they handle maintenance.
aws-c5-t06.example: A web app uses RDS MySQL Multi-AZ: primary in AZ-a, synchronous standby in AZ-b. If the primary fails, RDS fails over automatically.
keyPoints: Engines: Aurora, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server.
Automated backups (retention 1–35 days) and manual snapshots; point-in-time restore.
Multi-AZ: synchronous standby for high availability (failover).
Read replicas: asynchronous copies to scale reads.
Runs in a VPC; use security groups; encryption with KMS.
No OS/SSH access to the host.
commonMistakes: Thinking Multi-AZ improves read performance (that's read replicas).
Expecting SSH access to RDS.

examQuestions.question: Multi-AZ vs read replica.
examQuestions.answer: Multi-AZ: HA, synchronous, standby not readable (classic); replicas: scale reads, asynchronous.

examQuestions.question: Explain Amazon RDS.
examQuestions.answer: Managed relational DB service with engines, backups, HA.

knowledgeCheck.question: Primary DB fails; app continues. Feature?
RDS vs DB on EC2.
knowledgeCheck.answer: RDS managed; EC2 self-managed with full OS control.

aws-c5-t06.quickRevision: RDS: managed relational DB; Multi-AZ (HA, sync) vs read replicas (scale reads, async); backups 1–35 days.
aws-c5-t06.working: Create instance in a VPC subnet group; AWS manages backups/patches; Multi-AZ keeps a standby; replicas serve reads.

aws-c5-t07.title: Amazon Aurora
aws-c5-t07.definition: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL that offers higher performance and availability by using a distributed, self-healing storage layer.
aws-c5-t07.simpleExplanation: Aurora AWS ka apna cloud-native database hai, MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible. Storage khud badhta hai aur data 3 AZ me 6 copies me rehta hai, isliye bahut reliable aur fast.
aws-c5-t07.realLifeAnalogy: A high-performance version of a familiar car engine designed specifically for the AWS road.
aws-c5-t07.example: An online store uses Aurora with 1 writer and 3 read replicas; storage grows automatically as orders increase; failover takes seconds.
keyPoints: MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible.
Storage auto-scales from 10 GB up to 128 TiB.
Six copies of data across three AZs.
Up to 15 read replicas sharing the same storage.
Aurora Serverless scales capacity automatically.
Aurora Global Database for cross-Region replication.
commonMistakes: Believing Aurora is a separate non-SQL database; it is relational.
Saying 3 copies (it is 6).

examQuestions.question: Explain Amazon Aurora.
examQuestions.answer: Compatibility, storage layer, replicas, serverless.

examQuestions.question: Aurora vs RDS MySQL.
examQuestions.answer: Aurora has shared distributed storage, faster failover, more replicas; RDS MySQL uses EBS-based storage.

knowledgeCheck.question: Aurora vs DynamoDB.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Aurora is relational/SQL; DynamoDB is NoSQL key-value.

aws-c5-t07.quickRevision: Aurora: MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible, 6 copies/3 AZs, storage to 128 TiB, 15 replicas, serverless option.

aws-c5-t08.title: Amazon DynamoDB
aws-c5-t08.definition: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed, serverless NoSQL key-value and document database that provides single-digit-millisecond performance at any scale.
aws-c5-t08.simpleExplanation: DynamoDB ek NoSQL database hai: fixed schema nahi, key se data access. Serverless hai, bahut fast aur khud scale hota hai. Gaming, shopping carts, IoT ke liye achha.
aws-c5-t08.realLifeAnalogy: A giant dictionary: give the key and get the value instantly, no matter how big the dictionary is.
aws-c5-t08.example: Table Users with partition key userId. PutItem {userId:'u1', name:'Asha', city:'Pune'}; GetItem userId='u1' returns the item in milliseconds.
keyPoints: Table → items → attributes; primary key = partition key (+ optional sort key).
Capacity modes: on-demand and provisioned (RCU/WCU).
Secondary indexes: GSI and LSI.
Single-digit ms latency; DAX adds in-memory caching.
DynamoDB Streams for change capture; Global Tables for multi-Region.
Item size limit 400 KB.
commonMistakes: Using DynamoDB for complex joins.
Choosing a low-cardinality partition key causing hot partitions.

examQuestions.question: Explain DynamoDB.
examQuestions.answer: NoSQL, keys, capacity modes, indexes, streams.

examQuestions.question: DynamoDB vs RDS.
examQuestions.answer: Key-value NoSQL serverless scale vs relational SQL with joins.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is a partition key?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Attribute whose value decides the partition for an item.

knowledgeCheck.question: Shopping cart needing ms latency at scale. Service?
On-demand vs provisioned.
knowledgeCheck.answer: On-demand pays per request; provisioned reserves capacity.

aws-c5-t08.quickRevision: DynamoDB: serverless NoSQL, partition(+sort) key, ms latency, on-demand/provisioned, GSI/LSI, DAX, Streams.
aws-c5-t08.working: Requests hash the partition key to find the partition; data replicated across AZs.

aws-c5-t09.title: Amazon Redshift
aws-c5-t09.definition: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed, petabyte-scale cloud data warehouse that uses columnar storage and massively parallel processing for analytics (OLAP).
aws-c5-t09.simpleExplanation: Redshift data warehouse hai: bahut bada data par analytics aur reports ke liye. Column-based storage aur parallel processing se complex SQL queries tez chalti hain.
aws-c5-t09.realLifeAnalogy: A library for researchers: not for daily transactions at the counter, but great for studying huge archives quickly.
aws-c5-t09.example: A retailer loads years of sales from S3 into Redshift and runs a SQL query for monthly revenue by region in seconds.
keyPoints: Data warehouse for OLAP, not OLTP.
Columnar storage + MPP.
Cluster = leader node + compute nodes.
SQL (PostgreSQL-based) interface.
Redshift Spectrum queries data in S3.
Integrates with BI tools.
commonMistakes: Using Redshift for frequent small transactions.
Confusing it with a NoSQL store.

examQuestions.question: Redshift vs RDS.
examQuestions.answer: Redshift: OLAP analytics, columnar, MPP; RDS: OLTP row-based.

examQuestions.question: What is Redshift Spectrum?
examQuestions.answer: Querying data in S3 directly from Redshift.

knowledgeCheck.question: Analyse terabytes of sales history. Service?
OLTP vs OLAP.
knowledgeCheck.answer: OLTP: many small transactions; OLAP: complex analytical queries.

aws-c5-t09.quickRevision: Redshift: columnar MPP data warehouse for OLAP; leader+compute nodes; Spectrum queries S3.
aws-c5-t09.working: Leader plans query; compute nodes process slices in parallel; results aggregated.

aws-c5-t10.title: Launch an Amazon RDS DB Instance
aws-c5-t10.definition: Launching an RDS DB instance means choosing an engine, instance class, storage, credentials and network settings in the console, then connecting with a SQL client using the endpoint.
aws-c5-t10.simpleExplanation: Console: RDS → Create database → engine (MySQL) → Free tier template → identifier, master username/password → db.t3.micro → storage → VPC + security group (3306) → Create. Phir endpoint se connect karo.
aws-c5-t10.realLifeAnalogy: Booking a managed office: pick size, set the admin password, and use the address (endpoint) to enter.
aws-c5-t10.example: Create db 'mydb' (MySQL, db.t3.micro, 20 GB). Connect: mysql -h mydb.xxxx.ap-south-1.rds.amazonaws.com -u admin -p.
keyPoints: Steps: Create database → Standard create → engine → template (Free tier) → settings → instance class → storage → connectivity → create.
Master username/password required.
Public access: No for production; use SG to allow app only.
SG must allow DB port (3306/5432/1433).
Endpoint DNS name is used to connect.
Delete the instance (and skip final snapshot if not needed) to avoid charges.
commonMistakes: Opening 0.0.0.0/0 on the DB port.
Using the wrong endpoint or port.

examQuestions.question: Steps to launch an RDS DB instance.
examQuestions.answer: As listed.

examQuestions.question: Cannot connect to RDS. Why?
examQuestions.answer: SG not allowing port, public access/subnet routing, wrong endpoint or credentials.

knowledgeCheck.question: Production DB reachable from internet. Fix?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Disable public access; restrict SG to app tier.

knowledgeCheck.question: Free tier template vs production.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Free tier is single-AZ small; production uses Multi-AZ and larger classes.

aws-c5-t10.quickRevision: RDS lab: Create database → engine/template → credentials → class/storage → VPC+SG(port) → create → connect via endpoint.
aws-c5-t10.working: Console: RDS → Create database; wait until Available; copy endpoint; connect with client.

aws-c6-t01.title: Identity and Access Management
aws-c6-t01.definition: Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls who (authentication) can do what (authorisation) on which AWS resources, using users, groups, roles and policies.
aws-c6-t01.simpleExplanation: IAM me do cheezein: kaun ho (authentication) aur kya kar sakte ho (authorization). Users, groups, roles aur policies se permissions control hoti hain.
aws-c6-t01.realLifeAnalogy: A building's security system: ID card proves who you are, access rules decide which rooms you can enter.
aws-c6-t01.example: Create user 'asha' in group 'Developers' (policy: S3 read-only). An EC2 instance uses a role to write to S3 without storing keys.
keyPoints: User: a person/app with long-term credentials.
Group: collection of users; attach policies once for all.
Role: assumed identity with temporary credentials (for services, cross-account).
Policy: JSON document defining permissions.
Root user has full access: protect with MFA and avoid daily use.
Principle of least privilege.
mustKnow: User vs group vs role vs policy.
commonMistakes: Putting access keys inside EC2 instead of using a role.
Using root user for everyday work.

examQuestions.question: User vs group vs role.
examQuestions.answer: User: identity with credentials; group: set of users; role: temporary assumable identity.

examQuestions.question: Explain IAM basics.
examQuestions.answer: Authentication, authorisation, policies, least privilege.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is a policy?
knowledgeCheck.answer: A JSON document that defines permissions.

knowledgeCheck.question: EC2 must read S3 safely. Use?
knowledgeCheck.answer: IAM role attached to the instance

knowledgeCheck.question: Authentication vs authorisation.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Authentication proves identity; authorisation decides permissions.

aws-c6-t01.quickRevision: IAM: users (credentials), groups (sets), roles (temporary), policies (JSON); least privilege; protect root with MFA.

aws-c6-t02.title: AWS IAM
aws-c6-t02.definition: AWS IAM is the global AWS service that manages identities and permissions, offering MFA, password policies, access keys, federation and policy evaluation.
aws-c6-t02.simpleExplanation: AWS IAM free service hai, global hai. MFA, password policy, access keys, federation aur policy evaluation deta hai. Rule: explicit deny sabse upar, phir allow, warna default deny.
aws-c6-t02.realLifeAnalogy: The rulebook and ID desk for your whole AWS account.
aws-c6-t02.example: A company sets a password policy, enables MFA for all users and uses IAM roles for EC2. An explicit Deny on deleting S3 buckets overrides any Allow.
keyPoints: Global service; no extra cost.
Features: MFA, password policy, access keys, federation (SAML/OIDC), Access Analyzer, credential reports.
Policy evaluation: explicit Deny > explicit Allow > implicit Deny.
By default new users have no permissions.
Rotate access keys; prefer roles.
Root user best practices: MFA, no access keys.
commonMistakes: Thinking Allow beats Deny.
Sharing access keys.

examQuestions.question: Explain AWS IAM and its best practices.
examQuestions.answer: Features; least privilege; MFA; roles; rotate keys.

examQuestions.question: Evaluation order of policies?
examQuestions.answer: Explicit deny first, then explicit allow, else implicit deny.

knowledgeCheck.question: Default access for a new user:
Share access across accounts safely. Use?
Access key vs role.

aws-c6-t03.title: Implement IAM Policies
aws-c6-t03.definition: Implementing IAM policies means writing JSON statements (Effect, Action, Resource, Condition) and attaching them to users, groups or roles to grant least-privilege access.
aws-c6-t03.simpleExplanation: Policy JSON me likhte hain: kya allow/deny (Effect), kaunsa action, kaunsa resource, aur condition. Phir group/user/role se attach karte hain.
aws-c6-t03.realLifeAnalogy: Writing the rules on a visitor pass: who can enter which rooms and when.
aws-c6-t03.example: Policy: Allow s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on bucket my-bucket. Attach to group ReadOnlyS3, add user asha to the group, test with the Policy Simulator.
keyPoints: Policy elements: Version, Statement[Effect, Action, Resource, Condition].
Types: AWS managed, customer managed, inline.
Identity-based vs resource-based (bucket policy) vs permissions boundary.
Best practice: attach to groups, least privilege.
Use IAM Policy Simulator to test.
Conditions: MFA, source IP, time.
commonMistakes: Using '*' for Action/Resource unnecessarily.
Forgetting both bucket and object ARNs for S3.

examQuestions.question: Write an S3 read-only policy.
examQuestions.answer: JSON with Allow s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket on bucket and objects.

examQuestions.question: Managed vs inline policy.
examQuestions.answer: Managed reusable and attachable to many; inline embedded in one identity.

knowledgeCheck.question: Attaching policies to groups is a best practice.
Allow only from office IP. Use?
Identity-based vs resource-based.

aws-c6-t04.title: Monitoring Resources: AWS CloudWatch
aws-c6-t04.definition: Amazon CloudWatch collects metrics, logs and events from AWS resources and applications, and lets you create dashboards and alarms that trigger actions.
aws-c6-t04.simpleExplanation: CloudWatch AWS ka monitoring service hai: metrics (CPU), logs, alarms aur dashboards. Alarm threshold cross kare to SNS notification ya Auto Scaling action chala sakta hai.
aws-c6-t04.realLifeAnalogy: A dashboard of a car with warning lights: it shows speed and fuel and alerts when something goes wrong.
aws-c6-t04.example: Alarm: CPUUtilization > 80% for 2 consecutive 5-minute periods → send SNS email and trigger Auto Scaling.
keyPoints: Metrics: time-ordered data points (CPU, network, disk).
Basic monitoring 5 minutes; detailed monitoring 1 minute.
Memory/disk-usage needs the CloudWatch agent.
Alarms: OK, ALARM, INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
Logs: centralised log groups and streams.
CloudTrail records API calls (who did what); CloudWatch monitors performance.
commonMistakes: Expecting memory metrics by default.
Confusing CloudWatch with CloudTrail.

examQuestions.question: Explain CloudWatch features.
examQuestions.answer: Metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards, events.

examQuestions.question: CloudWatch vs CloudTrail.
examQuestions.answer: CloudWatch = performance monitoring; CloudTrail = API audit logging.

knowledgeCheck.question: EC2 memory usage is reported by default.

aws-c6-t04.quickRevision: CloudWatch: metrics, logs, alarms (OK/ALARM/INSUFFICIENT), dashboards; basic 5 min, detailed 1 min; CloudTrail audits API calls.
aws-c6-t04.purpose: Observe and react to resource health.
aws-c6-t04.working: Resources publish metrics; alarms evaluate thresholds; actions (SNS, Auto Scaling) triggered.

aws-c6-t05.title: Elastic Load Balancing (Scaling and Monitoring Context)
aws-c6-t05.definition: In the scaling context, Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic across healthy targets, supports connection draining and is monitored through CloudWatch metrics such as RequestCount and HealthyHostCount.
aws-c6-t05.simpleExplanation: Is chapter me ELB ko scaling aur monitoring ke saath dekhte hain: health checks, connection draining, sticky sessions aur CloudWatch metrics. (Syllabus me ye topic Chapter 3 me bhi hai.)
aws-c6-t05.realLifeAnalogy: A queue manager who also reports how busy each counter is.
aws-c6-t05.example: ALB metrics: RequestCount, TargetResponseTime, HealthyHostCount, HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count. If HealthyHostCount drops to 0, an alarm notifies the team.
keyPoints: Health checks decide eligible targets.
Connection draining (deregistration delay) lets in-flight requests finish.
Sticky sessions bind a user to a target.
SSL/TLS termination at the load balancer.
CloudWatch metrics for monitoring and scaling.
Works with Auto Scaling to add/remove targets automatically.
commonMistakes: Ignoring health-check path configuration.
Overusing sticky sessions that unbalance load.

examQuestions.question: Explain ELB role in scalable architecture.
examQuestions.answer: Distribution, health checks, draining, metrics, ASG.

examQuestions.question: What is connection draining?
examQuestions.answer: Allowing in-flight requests to complete before removing a target.

knowledgeCheck.question: Metric showing number of healthy targets:

knowledgeCheck.answer: Route a client to the same target.

knowledgeCheck.question: Deploying new instances without dropping requests. Feature?
Health check vs alarm.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Health check decides routing; alarm notifies/acts on metrics.
