aws-c6-t06.title: Auto Scaling (Policies and Cooldown Context)
aws-c6-t06.definition: In this chapter's context, Auto Scaling uses CloudWatch alarms and scaling policies, cooldown/warm-up periods and lifecycle hooks to adjust capacity safely.
aws-c6-t06.simpleExplanation: Auto Scaling CloudWatch alarm ke basis par instances add/remove karta hai. Cooldown period baar-baar scale hone se rokta hai. (Syllabus me ye topic Chapter 3 me bhi hai.)
aws-c6-t06.realLifeAnalogy: A thermostat with a delay so the AC doesn't switch on and off every second.
aws-c6-t06.example: Target tracking: keep average CPU at 50%. If CPU rises to 80%, ASG scales out; after the cooldown, if CPU falls below target, it scales in.
keyPoints: Policies: target tracking, step, simple, scheduled, predictive.
CloudWatch alarms drive step/simple policies.
Cooldown/warm-up prevents thrashing.
Lifecycle hooks pause instances for custom actions.
Scale-in protection protects chosen instances.
Costs follow actual capacity.
commonMistakes: Setting cooldown too short causing thrashing.
Using only scheduled scaling for unpredictable load.

examQuestions.question: Explain Auto Scaling policies and cooldown.
examQuestions.answer: Types, alarms, cooldown, hooks.

examQuestions.question: Why a cooldown period?
examQuestions.answer: To avoid launching/terminating instances too frequently.

knowledgeCheck.question: Policy that keeps a metric at a target value:
Purpose of lifecycle hook?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Pause instance launch/termination for custom actions.

knowledgeCheck.question: Step vs target tracking.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Step uses alarm thresholds with steps; target tracking auto-adjusts to hold a target.

aws-c6-t07.title: Cloud Economics and Billing
aws-c6-t07.definition: Cloud economics studies cost advantages of the pay-as-you-go model, and AWS billing tools (Pricing Calculator, Cost Explorer, Budgets) help estimate, track and control spending.
aws-c6-t07.simpleExplanation: Cloud me kharcha usage par depend karta hai. AWS ke tools se cost estimate, track aur control karte hain: Pricing Calculator, Cost Explorer, Budgets, tags, consolidated billing.
aws-c6-t07.realLifeAnalogy: A mobile bill: pay for usage, see itemised charges, set a limit alert so there are no surprises.
aws-c6-t07.example: Illustrative: if an instance costs $0.02/hour and runs 200 hours, cost = $4. Using Budgets, set an alert at 80% of a $50 monthly limit.
keyPoints: Pricing principles: pay-as-you-go, save when you commit (Reserved/Savings Plans), pay less by using more (volume discounts), pay less as AWS grows.
Free tier: 12-month, always-free and short trials.

Support plans: Basic, Developer, Business, Enterprise.
TCO compares on-prem vs cloud.
commonMistakes: Forgetting data transfer and EBS charges.
Leaving resources running.

aws-c6-t07.quickRevision: Economics: pay-as-you-go, commit to save, volume discounts; tools: Calculator, Cost Explorer, Budgets, tags, Organizations.

aws-c6-t08.title: Scale and Load Balance Your Architecture
aws-c6-t08.definition: Scaling and load balancing an architecture means combining an Application Load Balancer, an Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs and CloudWatch-driven policies so capacity follows demand with no single point of failure.
aws-c6-t08.simpleExplanation: Lab: Launch template banao, ALB aur target group banao, Auto Scaling group 2 AZ me banao, scaling policy lagao, load daal ke dekho instances badhte hain, aur end me cleanup.
aws-c6-t08.realLifeAnalogy: A restaurant chain adding counters automatically as the queue grows, with a manager directing people to the shortest queue.
aws-c6-t08.example: Launch template (web server AMI) → target group → ALB (2 public subnets) → ASG min 2, max 4, target CPU 50% → generate load → ASG scales out to 4 → remove load → scales in.
keyPoints: Create a launch template (AMI, type, SG, user data).
Create a target group and ALB across 2 AZs.
Create an Auto Scaling group using the template and attach the target group.
Add a target tracking scaling policy.
Test with load; watch CloudWatch and ASG activity history.
Clean up: delete ASG, ALB, target group, launch template.
commonMistakes: Putting the ALB in private subnets only.
Forgetting to delete resources afterwards.

examQuestions.question: Steps to scale and load balance an architecture.
examQuestions.answer: As listed.

examQuestions.question: How do you verify scaling?
examQuestions.answer: Generate load and watch ASG activity and CloudWatch metrics.

knowledgeCheck.question: ASG attaches to a target group.
One AZ fails. What happens?
knowledgeCheck.answer: ALB and ASG continue in the other AZ.

knowledgeCheck.question: ASG scale-out vs scale-in.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Out adds instances on high load; in removes them on low load.
